Reproduction: Bodyfat data (TH.data)

Source: vignettes/articles/reproduction-bodyfat.Rmd
reproduction-bodyfat.Rmd

Context

The bodyfat dataset from the TH.data package records body-composition and anthropometric measurements from 71 healthy German women. The response, DEXfat, is the percentage body fat measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA); the regressors include age, waist and hip circumference, elbow and knee breadth, and several derived anthropometric variables (anthro3a, anthro3b, anthro3c, anthro4). The original goal is to predict body fat from simpler anthropometric measurements.

Five of the reviewed works use this dataset under a Gamma distribution: Almuqrin and AbaOud (2025) [review23], Al-Ghamdi et al. (2025) [review44], Asar and Korkmaz (2022) [review51], Seifollahi et al. (2024) [review76] and El-Masry et al. (2025) [review127]. All of them state that they compute the condition number as the square root of the ratio between the largest and smallest eigenvalue of X′ŴXX'\hat{W}X.

Data 

library(multiCollglm)
if (!requireNamespace("TH.data", quietly = TRUE)) {
  knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
  message("The 'TH.data' package is not installed; skipping this article.")
}
data("bodyfat", package = "TH.data")
str(bodyfat)

mod <- glm(DEXfat ~ age + waistcirc + hipcirc + elbowbreadth + kneebreadth +
             anthro3a + anthro3b + anthro3c + anthro4,
           family = Gamma(link = "log"), data = bodyfat)
summary(mod)

Original diagnostic (a tour of the literature)

Almuqrin and AbaOud (2025), Al-Ghamdi et al. (2025) and El-Masry et al. (2025) report an identical value, CN=3394.30CN = 3394.30; none of them explicitly states which link function was used, so we could not reproduce that specific value. Asar and Korkmaz (2022) do specify a log link and untransformed data, and obtain CN=3410.63CN = 3410.63. Seifollahi et al. (2024) also claims to use a log link but reports a different value, CN=4026.23CN = 4026.23 – an inconsistency within the literature itself, since two works that claim to follow exactly the same procedure (Gamma, log, untransformed) do not agree with each other.

Diagnostic with multiCollglm 

methods <- c("RAW", "MP", "MS", "WS", "OZ")

tbl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(methods, function(m) {
  res <- tryCatch(condition_number(mod, method = m),
                   error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(res)) {
    data.frame(method = m, nc_label = NA, condition_number = NA,
               condition_index = NA)
  } else {
    data.frame(method = m, nc_label = res$nc_label,
               condition_number = res$condition_number,
               condition_index = res$condition_index)
  }
}))
knitr::kable(tbl, digits = 4)
method nc_label condition_number condition_index
RAW NC_RAW 1.163241e+07 3410.6317
MP NC_MP 1.239331e+05 352.0413
MS NC_MS 1.196367e+04 109.3785
WS NC_WS 1.239331e+05 352.0413
OZ NC_OZ 9.811259e+02 31.3229

A notable feature of this table: "MP" and "WS" agree exactly (not just approximately). The reason is structural, specific to this family/link combination: for a Gamma GLM with a log link, the IRLS weight of every observation at convergence is

wi=1V(μi)(dμidηi)2=1μi2⋅μi2=1,w_i = \frac{1}{V(\mu_i)}\left(\frac{d\mu_i}{d\eta_i}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{\mu_i^2}\cdot\mu_i^2 = 1,

i.e. constant and equal to 1 for every observation, regardless of the fitted values. This can be checked directly:

range(mod$weights)
#> [1] 1 1

With IRLS weights identically equal to 1, weighting by Ŵ1/2\hat{W}^{1/2} does nothing (it’s the same as the unweighted matrix), so rescaling to unit length before fitting ("MP") or after fitting ("WS") produces exactly the same matrix, and hence the same condition number. This is the log-link analogue, for Gamma, of the identity already documented for Gamma with the canonical inverse link (sqrt(w) * eta ≡ 1, see ?condition_number): every family/link combination has its own structural identity in the IRLS weights, and it is worth keeping in mind when interpreting any weighted collinearity diagnostic.

Comparison

Literature multiCollglm
Untransformed ("RAW") CN=3410.63CN = 3410.63 (Asar and Korkmaz 2022, square root) 3410.6317
Rescaled to unit length, no centering CN≈352.04CN \approx 352.04 352.0413
Centered + scaled ("OZ") – 31.3229

Asar and Korkmaz’s (2022) value reproduces with method = "RAW" to four decimal places: 3410.6317 versus their 3410.63. The “consensus” value from the other three works (3394.30) comes very close but not exactly, which suggests they used a slightly different link (or some minor sampling variant) that they did not document; and Seifollahi et al.’s (2024) value, despite claiming the same procedure as Asar and Korkmaz, is close to neither.

Conclusion

Once the already IRLS-weighted matrix is rescaled to unit length without centering ("WS"), the condition number drops from the thousands to a few hundred: the conclusion of severe collinearity holds, but is no longer dominated by the disparity in scale between variables as different as age (in years) and elbow breadth (in centimeters). The more interesting finding for this dataset, however, is the structural identity of the IRLS weights under Gamma with a log link: because they are always equal to 1, two of the package’s five methods coincide exactly, which does not happen in general for other family/link combinations (see the Nitrogen article, where none of the five methods agree with each other).
